slides.text: The kingdom of Aurelia had no sunsets. Every evening, just before the sky turned orange, the light simply vanished into night. Travelers thought it was a curse until they noticed something stranger: nobody in the kingdom ever seemed hopeless. They buried their dead smiling, faced wars without fear, and never mourned for long. It was as if grief itself had forgotten them.

An old librarian finally revealed the truth. Centuries ago, when a plague nearly destroyed the kingdom, the people begged the gods for one more chance. The gods agreed — but demanded every sunset in return. 'Why sunsets?' the king had asked. 'Because,' the gods replied, 'that's where humans hide their sadness. Without them, despair can never fully settle.'

On the day the ancient bargain finally expired, the kingdom witnessed its first sunset in six hundred years. People stopped in the streets as the sky caught fire with gold and crimson. Many wept without knowing why. The old librarian smiled through tears. 'Welcome back,' he whispered to the colors. 'We forgot how beautiful healing could look.'
